scope: Curated discovery library. Access and licenses apply to the named product, never automatically to every provider asset. No endorsement implied.

sources.title: The GDELT Project
sources.description: Machine-extracted events, mentions, themes, locations and tone support media-literacy exercises around climate and health reporting.
sources.access: Public bulk metadata, BigQuery and documented DOC/GEO APIs. Search availability can be intermittent; no live media result is required by core lessons.
sources.license: GDELT's own terms permit dataset reuse and redistribution with citation and a project link. These rights do not license publishers' articles, images or video.
sources.caveat: News mentions are not verified event counts, disease incidence or causation. Geocoding, language, outlet coverage and duplicated reporting introduce bias; sparse coverage does not mean low need.
sources.citation: The GDELT Project, named Event/Mentions/GKG or API product, extraction query, time window, release and access date; link original reports when checking claims.

sources.title: PovertyMaps.net / Meta Relative Wealth Index
sources.description: Berkeley/Meta microestimates describe relative living standards within countries at approximately 2.4 km resolution, with uncertainty.
sources.access: Country CSVs via HDX. The user-suggested PovertyMaps.net beta viewer currently redirects to an HTTP IP address; use the HTTPS HDX gateway for source data.
sources.license: Upstream HDX metadata specifies CC BY-NC 4.0. Preserve authors, license, changes and uncertainty; do not infer rights from a differently licensed derivative catalog.
sources.caveat: Relative wealth is not a dollar poverty threshold or household/clinic status, and raw scores are not directly comparable across countries. Paper coverage and downloadable release coverage differ; metadata update dates are not observation years.
sources.citation: Chi, G., Fang, H., Chatterjee, S., and Blumenstock, J.E. (2022). Microestimates of wealth for all low- and middle-income countries. PNAS 119(3), e2113658119. doi:10.1073/pnas.2113658119; cite selected HDX release.

sources.title: Gapminder: climate gaps and disparities
sources.description: Explore country indicators in Gapminder Tools and household examples in Dollar Street. Compare emissions, income and population with aligned years and denominators.
sources.access: Public tools and indicator downloads; trace each indicator to its original source.
sources.license: Covered Gapminder free materials and Dollar Street images: CC BY 4.0 with supplied credits. Underlying indicator and software licenses vary; do not infer blanket rights.
sources.caveat: Interpolated or extrapolated series are not all direct observations. Country means hide inequality; Dollar Street households are examples, not prevalence estimates. PPP-adjusted household consumption differs from salary or GDP.
sources.citation: Gapminder, selected tool/indicator, original provider, release and access date. Adapted material credit: Based on free material from GAPMINDER.ORG, CC-BY LICENSE.

sources.title: Global Nature Watch / Global Forest Watch
sources.description: WRI renamed Global Forest Watch to Global Nature Watch in September 2026; existing forest maps and dashboards continue within broader ecosystem monitoring.
sources.access: Public maps, layer metadata and downloads. Some analysis endpoints require API keys or OAuth; large rasters need an appropriate workflow.
sources.license: Named UMD tree-cover-loss and integrated-alert layers: CC BY 4.0. Other layer and platform rights vary. Tree-cover credit: Source: Hansen/UMD/Google/USGS/NASA.
sources.caveat: Tree-cover loss can reflect harvest, fire or natural disturbance, not necessarily deforestation. Alerts are investigation leads, not unbiased regional trend/area estimates. Tree gain can include plantations.
sources.citation: Hansen et al. (2013), doi:10.1126/science.1244693; tree-cover loss v1.13 through 2025, accessed 2026-10-09. Integrated alerts: UMD/GLAD and WUR, accessed through Global Nature Watch; retain exact version.

sources.title: Global Nature Watch Horizon
sources.description: A separate interface for exploring GNW and Land & Carbon Lab evidence through natural-language questions.
sources.access: External preview; no public integration API verified. Follow its source references back to the underlying data.
sources.license: Underlying dataset terms remain separate from interface and generated-summary rights. No platform output or imagery republished here.
sources.caveat: AI summaries can be incomplete or incorrect; verify figures, dates, place definitions and citations. A generated answer is not a validated local environmental assessment.
sources.citation: Global Nature Watch Horizon / WRI, underlying named dataset and exact cited release; record access date and any generated interpretation separately.

sources.title: An atlas of human suffering — public communication
sources.description: A Campaign against Climate Change response to the 2022 IPCC impacts assessment, useful for tracing public claims back to assessed evidence.
sources.access: Public article; linked reading only.
sources.license: No open reuse license verified. Do not copy the article's separately credited photograph.
sources.caveat: This is a secondary advocacy article, not an official IPCC atlas, dataset or independent scientific assessment.
sources.citation: Claire (2022-03-01). An atlas of human suffering: the latest IPCC report. Campaign against Climate Change.

sources.title: IPCC AR6: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability
sources.description: The 2022 Working Group II assessment provides the scientific context for climate impacts, adaptation options and vulnerability.
sources.access: Public report and chapter downloads; use official citations and chapter-specific confidence statements.
sources.license: IPCC/Cambridge publication rights and figure credits apply; this project links the report and writes its own synthesis.
sources.caveat: Preserve scenario, period, geography and assessed confidence. Global findings do not independently validate a local clinic model or attribute an individual disaster.
sources.citation: IPCC (2022). Climate Change 2022: Impacts, Adaptation and Vulnerability. Cambridge University Press. doi:10.1017/9781009325844.

sources.title: JRC World Atlas of Desertification
sources.description: Third-edition WAD3 maps overlapping land, water and socioeconomic concerns as starting points for local investigation.
sources.access: Public atlas, data catalog, convergence explorer and country reports; some legacy interactive endpoints can be intermittent.
sources.license: © European Union 2018; WAD3-JRC material reusable with source acknowledgement and preserved meaning. Third-party material retains separate rights. Named convergence dataset separately states CC BY 4.0.
sources.caveat: Convergence of issues is not measured land degradation, a current drought forecast or a health-risk score. Indicators span different historical periods and need local validation.
sources.citation: Cherlet, M., Hutchinson, C., Reynolds, J., Hill, J., Sommer, S., and von Maltitz, G. (eds.) (2018). World Atlas of Desertification, 3rd ed. Publications Office of the European Union. doi:10.2760/06292.

sources.title: University of Washington Global Refugee Atlas
sources.description: Origin–host connections, journey narratives, camp imagery and contextual indicators demonstrate multiple ways to communicate refugee experiences.
sources.access: Public atlas and source inventory; obtain analysis data from the original providers.
sources.license: No project-wide reuse license verified. Open-source dependencies do not license all photographs, narratives, geometry or underlying data. Link only.
sources.caveat: Its page titled Flow explains end-2018 refugee population stocks. Connections are not observed routes or annual movements and do not establish climate causation.
sources.citation: Zhao, B., Van Den Hoek, J., Alix-Garcia, J., Svevo, G., Baldrica-Franklin, G., and Katz, G. (2019). Global Refugee Atlas. University of Washington Humanistic GIS project.

sources.title: UNHCR forcibly displaced and stateless population maps
sources.description: Compare populations by origin, asylum and defined status; pair maps with official stock-versus-flow guidance.
sources.access: Public annex and data portal. Preserve the selected reference date; the inspected annex describes end-2025 data. Automated access can be rate limited.
sources.license: Refugee Data Portal datasets: CC BY 4.0 unless otherwise indicated; website design, software and logos excluded. Preserve original providers and disclose changes.
sources.caveat: Refugees, asylum-seekers, IDPs, returnees and stateless people have distinct definitions and can overlap. Stocks are not annual arrivals. These data alone cannot identify climate-attributable displacement.
sources.citation: UNHCR, Maps of forcibly displaced and stateless people, selected population group and reference date; underlying Refugee Data Portal release, accessed 2026-10-09.

sources.title: Atlas of Informality
sources.description: Selected informal-neighborhood boundaries at two historical dates support discussion of settlement change, heat, flooding and service access.
sources.access: Public ArcGIS map and mapping protocol; no geometry or photographs copied into this repository.
sources.license: Dataset license unspecified in inspected ArcGIS metadata. The linked 2020 article is CC BY 4.0; this does not establish rights for separate map geometry or images.
sources.caveat: Curated cases are not a complete settlement inventory. Boundary growth does not independently measure population, displacement, exposure or health-service access.
sources.citation: Samper, J., Shelby, J.A., and Behary, D. (2020). The Paradox of Informal Settlements Revealed in an ATLAS of Informality. Sustainability 12(22), 9510. doi:10.3390/su12229510.

sources.title: Atlas of Vulnerability: Developing Countries and the Pandemic
sources.description: Jubilee USA Network and LATINDADD compare economic, social, health and environmental conditions across 26 Latin American and Caribbean countries; database updated September 2024.
sources.access: Public indicator comparisons and exports; versions and indicator years differ.
sources.license: No explicit open reuse license verified. Download availability does not grant redistribution permission; check original indicator terms.
sources.caveat: This is a regional indicator dashboard, not a global climate score. Latest-available values can refer to different years; align units, dates, denominators and missingness before comparison.
sources.citation: Jubilee USA Network and LATINDADD. Atlas of Vulnerability: Developing Countries and the Pandemic. Database updated September 2024; accessed 2026-10-09.

sources.title: Surgo Africa COVID-19 Community Vulnerability Index
sources.description: The 2021 release compares seven vulnerability themes across 756 admin-1 regions in 48 countries.
sources.access: Public dashboard and archived Zenodo dataset; cross-country scores cover 36 countries because source differences restrict comparability.
sources.license: Archived dataset: CC BY-NC 4.0; dashboard content separately reserves rights. No index data copied here.
sources.caveat: Relative rankings depend on comparison scope; they are not infection probabilities, current burden or individual risk. Facility-per-capita indicators do not identify PEPFAR-supported facilities.
sources.citation: Mishra, A., et al. (2021). Africa COVID-19 Community Vulnerability Index (CCVI). Zenodo, published 28 April 2021. doi:10.5281/zenodo.4725492.

sources.title: World Bank Global Subnational Poverty Atlas
sources.description: GSAP supplies survey-based poverty estimates aligned to common years, principally at admin-1 scale. Current catalog identifies the AM26 / September 2026 vintage.
sources.access: Public map, downloadable tables and polygons. The linked map selects a 2023 estimate, not a 2023 PPP base.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 plus World Bank published additional terms; preserve release, original sources and transformations. No household-microdata access is implied.
sources.caveat: The $3.00 threshold is per person per day in 2021 PPP international dollars, not nominal USD. Area poverty rates do not identify individual poverty, clinic vulnerability or climate-caused displacement.
sources.citation: World Bank (2026). Global Subnational Poverty Atlas, AM26/September 2026 vintage; $3.00/day, 2021 PPP; reference year 2023. Accessed 2026-10-09.

sources.title: GEM Global Economic Vulnerability Map
sources.description: Version 2020.1 combines country-level economic exposure and resilience indicators in an earthquake-oriented framework covering 136 countries.
sources.access: Public product description and OpenQuake viewer; linked comparison only.
sources.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. This license remains separate from the repository's original materials.
sources.caveat: An earthquake economic-vulnerability index is not a climate-risk forecast or facility assessment. The source page's PDF/citation text refers inconsistently to the social-vulnerability product; use the economic title, version and DOI.
sources.citation: Burton, C., and Toquica, M. (2020). Global Economic Vulnerability Map, version 2020.1. doi:10.13117/GEM-ECONOMIC-VULNERABILITY-MAP.

sources.title: NASA GISTEMP v4
sources.description: Global annual land–ocean temperature anomalies, with raw source snapshot and provenance.
sources.access: Packaged CSV; public NASA tables.
sources.license: NASA scientific data; cite GISTEMP Team and the dataset methods paper.
sources.caveat: Anomaly relative to 1951–1980; global average is not a clinic temperature or personal heat exposure.
sources.citation: GISTEMP Team (2026), GISS Surface Temperature Analysis v4; Lenssen et al. (2024), doi:10.1029/2023JD040179. Accessed 2026-10-09.

sources.title: Healthsites.io / OpenStreetMap
sources.description: 155 unique OSM point features selected from the original repository's Healthsites archive across seven teaching contexts, including Mumbai.
sources.access: Local GeoJSON and provenance; Healthsites services for fresh data.
sources.license: Open Database License 1.0. © OpenStreetMap contributors, via Healthsites.io. Derivative database obligations apply.
sources.caveat: Original extraction date unknown. Selected point features are incomplete; location does not establish current operation, service availability or PEPFAR funding.
sources.citation: Healthsites.io / OpenStreetMap contributors. Selected archived World-node features from 2024-Climate-Heat-Stress; processed 2026-10-09. Original OSM node IDs retained.

sources.title: Copernicus Data Space STAC
sources.description: Search bounded Sentinel-2 L2A scene footprints and asset metadata; Mumbai example included.
sources.access: Public metadata search; asset downloads can have separate authentication requirements.
sources.license: Copernicus Sentinel Data Legal Notice; collection declares license identifier 'other'. Preserve acquisition and source credit.
sources.caveat: Reflectance is not air temperature. A footprint does not show hazard extent; cloud fraction for a whole scene does not describe a specific clinic pixel.
sources.citation: Copernicus Sentinel-2 data, ESA / European Commission, accessed via Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem; exact scene identifiers and access date in export.

sources.title: Digital Earth Africa
sources.description: WOfS annual water observations and Sentinel-2 GeoMAD metadata; Beira WOfS example included.
sources.access: Public STAC metadata and cloud-hosted assets; advanced raster analysis can use the DEA Sandbox.
sources.license: Named WOfS and GeoMAD products: CC BY 4.0, with product acknowledgements including modified Copernicus data for GeoMAD.
sources.caveat: Wet/clear observation frequency is not flood probability, depth or water quality. Preserve valid-observation counts, clouds, acquisition period and CRS.
sources.citation: Digital Earth Africa Water Observations from Space annual summary, 2022, accessed 2026-10-09; exact item identifiers in snapshot. Cite the selected product specifications.

sources.title: Allen Coral Atlas
sources.description: Eight actual benthic habitat polygons near Mombasa, served from the provider's public WFS. They complement the synthetic thermal-stress lesson.
sources.access: Public WFS/WMS; some downloads require registration. No global Atlas dataset or Planet mosaic is republished here.
sources.license: Mapped habitat products: CC BY 4.0; separate Planet imagery terms include CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Consult provider conditions for global redistribution.
sources.caveat: Habitat classification is not observed bleaching, current ecological condition or fish production. This first-page extract is not representative coverage.
sources.citation: Allen Coral Atlas (2022), Imagery, maps and monitoring of the world's tropical coral reefs. doi:10.5281/zenodo.3833242. Allen Coral Atlas Partnership / Arizona State University. Bounded extract accessed 2026-10-09.

sources.title: NOAA Coral Reef Watch
sources.description: Satellite sea-surface temperature and thermal-stress products; methodology informs the course's synthetic 84-day Degree Heating Week exercise.
sources.access: Public product and methodology pages; no operational NOAA reef observations are bundled in the DHW exercise.
sources.license: NOAA public-domain data, with NOAA Coral Reef Watch attribution and product-specific citation.
sources.caveat: Thermal stress indicates exposure, not directly observed bleaching. Do not substitute CoralWatch chart scores for satellite DHW.
sources.citation: NOAA Coral Reef Watch: cite exact product, version, dates and recommended publication from its citation guidance.

sources.title: CoralWatch citizen science
sources.description: Twenty coral colour observations from one public Random Survey at Abu Sawatyr, Red Sea, Egypt. Personal fields and precise coordinates omitted.
sources.access: Packaged CSV plus public BioCollect survey; published eventDate retained verbatim.
sources.license: This Random Survey explicitly states CC BY 4.0. Other survey types can use CC BY-NC 2.5: never generalize this license to the entire portal.
sources.caveat: Scores are a descriptive chart index, not percent bleaching, coral cover or a representative reef estimate. Schema checks do not independently verify field observations.
sources.citation: CoralWatch (2026), Random Survey bd39e449-038f-4d45-ab6d-b56922a6f532, Abu Sawatyr, Egypt. 20-observation reduced extract, accessed 2026-10-09. Changes documented in packaged metadata.

sources.title: Climate Central coastal tools
sources.description: Coastal Risk Finder, CoastalDEM, coastal flood layers and portfolio screening support advanced coastal questions.
sources.access: Use public tools; data packages and commercial products require the applicable negotiated access or license.
sources.license: Product-specific Climate Central terms. No CoastalDEM raster, proprietary flood layer or restricted portfolio dataset is bundled.
sources.caveat: Elevation threshold maps require datum, connectivity, uncertainty, defenses and time-horizon checks before inferring inundation or facility disruption.
sources.citation: Climate Central: cite selected tool or product, model version, scenario, horizon and access date.

sources.title: AlphaEarth.ai — carbon-market platform
sources.description: The user-suggested alphaearth.ai domain is a carbon-market intelligence platform operated by Crelocks LLC.
sources.access: Subscription and platform-specific access.
sources.license: Provider terms; no redistribution permission inferred and no platform dataset copied.
sources.caveat: This domain is distinct from Google / Google DeepMind's AlphaEarth Foundations satellite embeddings.
sources.citation: AlphaEarth.ai, Crelocks LLC. Platform and terms accessed 2026-10-09.

sources.title: Google AlphaEarth Foundations
sources.description: Annual 10 m satellite embeddings with 64 dimensions for environmental pattern analysis, available through Earth Engine and a public cloud bucket.
sources.access: Earth Engine account or documented public GCS access; large tiles need a suitable processing environment.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0. Required credit: The AlphaEarth Foundations Satellite Embedding dataset is produced by Google and Google DeepMind.
sources.caveat: Embedding dimensions are not temperature, disease, carbon or habitat measurements. Validate any downstream classifier; preserve exact tile and year availability.
sources.citation: Google and Google DeepMind, Satellite Embedding V1 Annual; Brown et al. (2025), doi:10.48550/arXiv.2507.22291. Cite the exact release and tiles used.

sources.title: Global Fishing Watch
sources.description: Explore apparent fishing effort and maritime activity as livelihood and ecosystem context.
sources.access: Public map; API requires a personal bearer token. No API token is embedded in the site.
sources.license: Public API terms include CC BY-NC 4.0 plus dataset-specific conditions. Required attribution: Powered by Global Fishing Watch.
sources.caveat: Modeled apparent fishing hours are not catch, illegal activity or dietary intake. AIS coverage favors larger vessels and misses much artisanal activity.
sources.citation: Global Fishing Watch, exact dataset/version and period; cite API terms and methods. Powered by Global Fishing Watch.

sources.title: FEWS NET food-security outlooks
sources.description: Acute food insecurity maps and outlooks provide regional livelihood and nutrition context.
sources.access: Public map and geographic-data downloads; retain issue date, target period and assessed versus projected status.
sources.license: Dataset-specific FEWS NET use and attribution policy; do not assume a blanket Creative Commons license.
sources.caveat: An ordinal area phase is not every household's outcome and must not be averaged into a disease-risk score. IPC-compatible analyses are not necessarily IPC consensus products.
sources.citation: FEWS NET, country, product, issue date, assessment/projection period, URL and access date; include credited partner sources.

sources.title: WRI Aqueduct Water Risk Atlas 4.0
sources.description: Baseline and future water-risk indicators for comparing explicitly defined basin-level conditions.
sources.access: Public map, data downloads and indicator dictionary.
sources.license: CC BY 4.0 for the named Aqueduct 4.0 data; credit WRI and original providers.
sources.caveat: Baseline water stress measures demand relative to renewable supply, not tap-water safety or clinic water availability. Raw indicators, normalized scores and future scenarios are distinct.
sources.citation: Kuzma et al. (2023), Aqueduct 4.0: Updated decision-relevant global water risk indicators. WRI, doi:10.46830/writn.23.00061.

sources.title: IOM environmental migration resources
sources.description: Migration Data Portal, IOM environmental migration resources and DTM climate-and-mobility material support careful interpretation of movement and immobility.
sources.access: External portals; some pages can restrict automated access. Select an explicitly documented underlying dataset before analysis.
sources.license: Dataset- and publication-specific IOM/provider terms. Linked references only here.
sources.caveat: Stocks, flows, displacement events and unique people differ. Migration is multicausal; movement does not automatically confer refugee status. Avoid identifiable routes or vulnerable-person locations.
sources.citation: IOM / Migration Data Portal / DTM, exact named product, location, reporting period, release and access date.

sources.title: Climate Conflict Vulnerability Index
sources.description: A quarterly 0.5-degree composite index for investigating interacting contextual vulnerabilities.
sources.access: Public maps and release-specific scores; raw indicator availability and historical release corrections vary.
sources.license: Data: CC BY-NC 4.0. Software: GPL 3.0. These are separate rights; no index data bundled here.
sources.caveat: An expert-weighted index is not a calibrated probability of violence or evidence that climate causes conflict. Check input dates, missingness, scale and release corrections; never rank patients or communities with it.
sources.citation: Climate Conflict Vulnerability Index, University of the Bundeswehr Munich / PIK / German Federal Foreign Office; cite exact quarterly release and methodology.

sources.title: Climate change and mass atrocities: a research frontier
sources.description: A discussion prompt about pathways, institutions, prevention and uncertainty, paired with current scientific evidence.
sources.access: Public museum article; no dataset or figures copied.
sources.license: USHMM terms; linked reference and original summary only.
sources.caveat: A 2017 research commentary is not a current risk forecast, causal model or operational targeting layer.
sources.citation: Blatt, Charlotte (2017-08-16). Climate Change and Mass Atrocities: A New Research Frontier. United States Holocaust Memorial Museum.

sources.title: Sponge cities and green infrastructure
sources.description: Connect permeable surfaces, storage, vegetation and drainage to the adaptation lesson's auditable rainfall-volume calculation.
sources.access: Background encyclopedia and primary environmental guidance; no copied maps or text.
sources.license: Wikipedia text has its own share-alike terms; primary guidance retains provider rights. Original course exercise is separately licensed.
sources.caveat: Storage capacity alone cannot predict flood prevention. Consider infiltration, saturation, maintenance, drainage, mosquitoes, accessibility and tradeoffs in pollen exposure.
sources.citation: Cite the exact design guidance and local hydrologic evidence used. Wikipedia is a background orientation, not a substitute for engineering validation.

sources.title: Nature-based solutions for climate change mitigation
sources.description: Conservation, restoration and ecosystem management as climate mitigation, with safeguards and limits.
sources.access: Public UNEP report; linked reading and original course synthesis.
sources.license: Report-specific UNEP/IUCN rights and third-party credits. Figures are not republished here.
sources.caveat: Mitigation potential is not a guaranteed local health benefit or a substitute for emissions reductions. Test biodiversity, tenure, livelihoods, maintenance and distributional impacts.
sources.citation: UNEP and IUCN (2021). Nature-based solutions for climate change mitigation. Published 4 November 2021.

sources.title: WHO / WMO Atlas of Health and Climate
sources.description: Joint meteorological and public-health cases spanning infections, emergencies, environmental conditions and preparedness.
sources.access: WHO, TDR and WMO landing pages point to the same 2012 work. Linked reference, no copied figures.
sources.license: Current WHO page states CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO, while original PDF says © WHO/WMO 2012 all rights reserved and credits third-party figures. Treat illustrations individually.
sources.caveat: Historical synthesis: update epidemiology and current climate evidence separately. WHO and WMO landing-page dates differ; the publication year is 2012.
sources.citation: WHO and WMO (2012). Atlas of Health and Climate. 64 pp. ISBN 9789241564526; WMO-No.1098.

sources.title: Malaria Atlas Project
sources.description: Explore malaria incidence, prevalence, interventions and uncertainty, using small country/admin summaries before global raster analysis.
sources.access: Public platform and documented HTTP access guide; select an explicit release, species, indicator and denominator.
sources.license: MAP maps explicitly CC BY 3.0; original survey/provider rights remain separate. Cite the exact data layer and associated publication.
sources.caveat: Modeled estimates are not surveillance case counts or climate-attributable cases. Validate zero-versus-missing conventions and whether a metric has genuine uncertainty bounds.
sources.citation: Malaria Atlas Project, exact dataset/layer and publication, species, release, year, URL and access date. Do not cite only the portal for an analysis.

sources.title: EAACI Global Atlas of Planetary Health
sources.description: Climate, air pollution, allergy, asthma, pollen, healthcare sustainability and nature-based solutions broaden the clinical pathways in the course.
sources.access: Public 2025 atlas PDF; v1.2 appears in the supplied filename, not an independently verified edition statement.
sources.license: No blanket open license verified; figure-specific permissions differ. Linked reference and original synthesis, no figures copied.
sources.caveat: A clinical-science atlas is not a geospatial dataset or local asthma predictor. Urban planting can have seasonal pollen tradeoffs; assess locally appropriate species and exposure.
sources.citation: Akdis, C., Agache, I., Nadeau, K.C., and Pali-Schöll, I. (eds.) (2025). Global Atlas of Planetary Health. European Academy of Allergy and Clinical Immunology.

sources.title: ClimaHealth / Wellcome Climate Change Impact Map
sources.description: Wellcome's country explorer combines historical climate, disaster impacts and climate-sensitive disease literature; ClimaHealth provides the discovery entry.
sources.access: Public interactive dashboard. No underlying CRU or EM-DAT data copied into this repository.
sources.license: Wellcome website default CC BY 4.0 does not override upstream rights. CRU data: ODbL / Database Contents License. EM-DAT: registration and restrictive product-specific terms.
sources.caveat: Historical interface series extend through 2021 and use a 1991–2020 anomaly baseline; literature panel covers 2013–2020. Missing disaster records do not establish no event or no harm.
sources.citation: Wellcome (2022-07-05). Tracking the health effects of climate change around the world; Climate and Health Dashboard v15. Discovered via ClimaHealth; accessed 2026-10-09.
